assessment.rationale: This simulation is a meta-spec-format candidate, not a UDP-feed/session protocol design, so it only partially fits the scenario. Its main value here is that it explicitly tries to require explanatory sections when layer composition is load-bearing, which helps boundary clarity and keeps specs small. But it does not define the applicability criteria, composition evidence, or failure cases needed to show that a UDP-feed API is sufficient for an upper session layer without leakage.
strengths: Targets layer-dependent explanatory sections instead of unconditional boilerplate.
Small and durable spec shape; easy to implement in constrained environments.
Improves chances that composition concerns are documented when truly load-bearing.
weaknesses: Does not directly specify UDP-feed v0 or session-layer composition behavior.
Applicability criteria are intentionally unresolved, weakening audit consistency.
Little explicit treatment of failure handling, adversarial pressure, or sparse-knowledge effects in this scenario.
risks: Authors may wrongly mark composition-related sections as not applicable and hide real cross-layer coupling.
Lack of explicit applicability criteria can reduce comparability across specs and audits.
open_questions: What concrete applicability test would force session-layer composition sections when UDP-feed binding details leak upward?
Can conditional sections be audited consistently across authors without a stricter checklist?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
